title: Kinetic sprint ops and people snapshot
summary: Leadership update focused on operational resilience, minor incident trends, temporary expansion of SRE headcount, hiring priorities for Q2, and a short Q&A about redistribution of on-call load and manager skip-level syncs.
action_items: Jonah: circulate updated on-call rotas and the new runbook by 2026-02-10
Priya: finalize 3 hiring scorecards for inference infra roles by 2026-02-17
Aisha: publish internal guidance on manager skip-levels and psychological safety check-ins by 2026-02-12

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-03 16:00 PT
Duration: 1:02:00
Attendees: Elena G., Marcus L., Priya N., Jonah R., Aisha K., entire company (all-hands)
Shared artifacts: link to slide deck (internal: /slides/ops-kinetic-2026-02-03.pdf), hiring tracker (sheet link), incident heatmap spreadsheet.

00:00 Elena: Hey everyone, welcome — thanks for hopping on. we wanted to keep this tight, about an hour, a check-in on ops and people. quick agenda up front.
00:18 Marcus: thanks. I'll kick off with a short state of infra and the recent perf incidents, then Jonah will do triage notes. Priya will cover hiring and ramp, Aisha will do people pulse.
00:34 Marcus: ok, so infra. over the last 30 days we saw three medium-severity incidents, none of them user-visible for long but they did affect ded- capacity scheduling. the root cause on two was a mismatch in auto-scale policy and our newer model variants — so basically Redwood Dedicate pools were overcommitted when sequence lengths spiked.
01:05 Marcus: we rolled a hotfix to the autoscaler, updated the kernel selection rules so the runtime prefers lower-quant variants on burst traffic, and added an alert for average kv cache miss rate. note: kv cache sometimes appears as "k v" in logs so we updated label parsing.
01:30 Speaker 2: Quick clarification — is this a model-agnostic change or specific to the llama-sim family?
01:37 Marcus: mostly model-agnostic; the selector looks at token distribution and tail latency. for the llama-sim infra, we did add a small profile tweak but it shouldn't be invasive.
01:50 Jonah: i'll take triage. two incidents were capacity contended, one was a scheduler race in the private deployment shim — the shim mis-reported backpressure to the control plane. that one required rolling the shim and a quick checkout of the fallback policies.
02:12 Jonah: on-call handled these per runbook, but we saw slower escalation in one case where the pager notes weren't specific enough about the first mitigation step — so we updated the runbook and added a one-line checklist to the PagerDuty flow.
02:28 Jonah: action: i'll distribute the updated runbook, and we will run a table-top drill next Tuesday to validate the path.
02:40 Elena: thanks Jonah — appreciate the crispness. a high-level ask: can we reduce noise while still keeping eyes on real capacity issues?
02:55 Jonah: yes. we're tuning thresholds, consolidating duplicate alerts from two tracing sources, and adding a short cooldown so we don't page on the same noisy metric.
03:10 Priya: hiring — quick snapshot. we're green on engineering hires: offers out to two infra staff engineers, one acceptance pending. main gap is in SRE and inference infra, especially folks with GPU performance background.
03:28 Priya: proposed: fast-track three IC roles and one senior SRE manager for Q2; prepping scorecards and interview kits. we've got a bit of friction on interview bandwidth, so we might borrow a rotation of principals to help panel.
03:45 Aisha: from People: candidate experience has improved, time-to-offer down to 12 days. retention: voluntary churn remains low but we see early tenure attrition in the 3-9 month band; exit notes often mention onboarding clarity and support for first-incidents.
04:05 Aisha: we're going to pilot a "first-incident buddy" program — pair a new hire with a 90-day buddy to walk the incident runbooks and who to ping.
04:20 Marcus: small ask — can product and trust teams add a short blurb to the onboarding doc about private deployment quirks (VPC, KMS integration steps)? folks new to infra are bumping into those.
04:33 Priya: will do; i'll add a checklist item to the onboarding playbook and point to the KMS FAQ.
04:40 Elena: ok moving to resilience bets. we have three near-term bets: 1) reduce mean time to mitigate for medium incidents by 30% through better runbooks and drills, 2) invest in observability around quantized inference paths, and 3) hire SRE capacity for rotational shadowing of production.
05:05 Elena: we'll measure burn using the incident heatmap and on-call load per person; Jonah, can you publish a weekly on-call load metric?
05:14 Jonah: yes i'll publish that and a histogram of pages per person.
05:20 Speaker 3: question — will this affect Dedicated vs Hosted routing policy in the console? meaning, if we increase cooldowns will Hosted API customers see throttling?
05:33 Marcus: good question. our routing policy will remain user-facing same; internal throttles are conservative and we've added fallback model variants to avoid user-level throttling. the cooldown is on alerting/paging, not on request routing.
05:48 Speaker 4: can you say more about the "fallback model variants"?
05:52 Marcus: we maintain lighter quantized variants for most models. when capacity spikes, smart routing will prefer a compatible variant — lower cost, slightly different quality trade-off; we surface that in logs and product metrics.
06:05 Priya: on the hiring side, this is why we need infra folks with quantization experience. it's pretty specialized.
06:15 Aisha: people pulse quick: anonymous survey showed 72% positive on manager support, but 42% reported feeling overloaded this sprint. we're adjusting scope and advocating for fewer concurrent initiatives.
06:28 Elena: management tip — please work with your leads to prune non-essential goals. aim to keep sprint WIP lower. we'll track this next sprint.
06:40 Jonas(?) // transcription note: speaker label fuzzy
06:44 Jonah: also recommended: rotate on-call blocks to 1 week for engineers in infra teams, not 24/7 day increments, to reduce sleep disruption.
06:55 Aisha: legal/HR note — we updated the mental health benefit reminder and will run two facilitated discussions about boundaries.
07:06 Speaker 5: question about comp and hiring bands — are we staying aggressive on market?
07:12 Elena: yes, we want to be competitive; but we're also prioritizing role fit and bar. compensation adjustments go through the hiring committee — Aisha's team will share updated ranges in the hiring tracker.
07:26 Priya: quick ops ask — can product PMs give a heads-up when they plan to add throughput testing to the staging lab? last minute tests have clobbered shared GPU capacity.
07:38 Marcus: yes, and also a reminder to use the quota tags and to book large runs. we added quota-tagging to the console last quarter but adoption is still spotty.
07:50 Speaker 6: clarify — quota tags, is that per team or per project?
07:55 Marcus: per project, but billing and routing uses per-team tag for cost breakdowns.
08:05 Elena: ok quick community Q&A — three questions we surfaced from Slack. first: what is the leadership view on dedicated vs private expansion for this year?
08:20 Elena: short answer: continue both tracks. Dedicated for mid-market customers that need reserved capacity and stability; Private is strategic for regulated customers. product will keep feature parity where possible, but rollout cadence may differ.
08:36 Second Q: will we open another hub for APAC infra?
08:41 Marcus: roadmap has APAC region for staging and lower-cost edge next quarter; production regions depend on demand signals from sales.
08:50 Third Q: any changes to benefits or flexible work?
08:54 Aisha: no structural changes this quarter, but we're piloting a flexible-day fund to support caregiving and unexpected needs. details in the People channel.
09:10 Elena: recap and ask. we have three tactical asks: 1) Jonah publish on-call load metric, 2) Priya finalize hiring scorecards, 3) Aisha publish manager skip-level guidance. we also pledged two chaos drills next week, and a hiring prioritization doc by Friday.
09:30 Elena: closing note — thank you team, small set of bets, aim for less context switching and more postmortem follow-through.
09:40 Audience applause / emoji flood (company chat)
09:50 End of recorded section; open floor for a few chat Qs and short manager breakouts.

Post-meeting notes (auto):
- Recording uploaded to internal drive.
- Slides and hiring tracker attached to the meeting thread.
- Action items assigned as above.
